claims.text: The as-cast or processed (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The untreated alloy has a large intrinsic caloric response.
The untreated alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is sensitive to cracking.
The proposed intervention is solutionizing at approximately 1000°C followed by aging at 500–600°C in an inert atmosphere.
Solutionizing at approximately 1000°C will homogenize the target alloy's microstructure.
Aging at 500–600°C will induce fine-scale second-phase precipitation in the target alloy.
The precipitated second phase will be ductile and load-bearing.
A fine, ductile second phase will blunt or impede crack initiation and propagation.
Nanoscale microstructural deformation or toughening mechanisms near a crack tip can contribute to alloy toughness.
The heat treatment will increase tensile strength, ductility, fracture toughness, crack-propagation resistance, or overall load-bearing integrity relative to the untreated alloy.
The heat treatment will reduce cracking relative to the untreated alloy.
The parent matrix will remain largely responsible for the alloy's caloric response after precipitation.
The heat treatment will preserve the caloric response under applied magnetic fields relative to the untreated alloy.
The heat treatment will preserve the caloric response under applied pressure fields relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed mechanical benefits are expected to apply from cryogenic to ambient temperatures.
The proposed benefits are expected under moderate magnetic fields, moderate pressures, and service-relevant mechanical loads.
The aging time and precise temperature window will control precipitate volume fraction and distribution and may affect caloric performance.
The long-term stability of the precipitated phase during cyclic refrigeration operation is uncertain.
